svg.title: Svalbard full-chip block diagram with tentative physical placement
svg.desc: Portrait die with RF on the west, wired PHY on the east, quiet clock circuits on the north and digital transport on the south. Fifty edge terminals remain allocated. Block sizes and pad locations are provisional.

g.text: Refinement 1 · short sensitive nets, local clocks / references, separated aggressors
Nominal 3.05 × 4.24 mm core envelope · 12.92 mm² ceiling
Custom pad / ESD / seal-ring region — fit and actual core boundary unproven
Sample clock dividers / update timing / CDC
Framing / packing / CDC · bounded queues · calibration / resource ownership · reset / faults
SPI / reset pad circuits on this domain
Nearby DDR registers and local returns
Check skew across HOST_A / B boundary
01 Keep the GHz paths at their pads
RF on the west; wired on the east. Put ESD,
input matching / termination and output drivers
at the boundary. No long raw RF or line nets.
RF PLL above the mixers; wired PLL above the
lane. Keep loop filters beside pump / VCO.
Route buffered reference clocks between islands;
do not share high-impedance tuning nodes.
03 Converters form the analog / digital seam
Place I/Q pairs together with symmetric loads.
Face analog terminals toward baseband; route
codes south. Reference buffers and reservoirs
stay local to the conversion load.
04 Put switching activity toward the south
Host pads sit beside their DDR registers.
Keep A / B supply segments and local returns.
Memory and gearboxes sit between host and
analog islands; avoid digital routes over VCOs.
05 Keep room for the real implementation
Blank lanes reserve routing / decoupling space.
Isolation structures are not designed here.
Bias trunks feed local buffers; diagnostics use
No added monitor, loop-filter or supply pins.
WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT ESTABLISH
Block areas are illustrative, not sized macros.
Die / nominal core aspect ratios follow the plan.
Custom pads may change the usable boundary.
Bond-wire, thermal and substrate coupling can
Narrow operating range does not remove these risks.
Solid arrows: selected local data paths. Dashed purple: selected clock / reference paths. Shared-service fanout is omitted for legibility.
Blocks include local bias / decoupling obligations; no blanket on-chip LDO or shielding topology is assumed. RF receive and transmit remain separate chains.
Next physical decision: size actual macros, trial a custom pad ring, then compare extracted clock/RF coupling and package return paths.
Conceptual placement only — this diagram does not start transistor layout or bypass mathematical and schematic closure.
